title: agnim īḷe purohitaṃ
about: The first verse of the Ṛgveda, India's oldest text, praises Agni, the fire that carries offerings up to the gods, and the last verse of the same hymn asks him to stay close. Printed without the Vedic pitch accents: ḷ (ळ) is the old Vedic sound of ḍ between vowels, piteva fuses pitā + iva, and 'gne is agne with its a swallowed after e (ऽ).

badge.name: First Verse
badge.about: Read the opening of the Ṛgveda

lines.en: I praise Agni, the household priest,
god of the sacrifice, the priest of the rite,
the invoker, best bestower of treasure.

q.prompt: What gift is Agni praised for?

lines.g: स नः पितेव सूनवे ऽग्ने सूपायनो भव
lines.t: sa naḥ piteva sūnave 'gne sūpāyano bhava
lines.en: So, Agni, be easy to reach for us, as a father is for his son.

q.prompt: How should Agni be towards his worshippers?
options: easy to reach, like a father to his son

lines.en: Stay with us, for our well-being.

title: karmaṇy evādhikāras te
about: On the battlefield of Kurukṣetra, Kṛṣṇa tells the warrior Arjuna to act without craving the result, the Gītā's most quoted verse. Words are printed apart: karmaṇy is karmaṇi with i turned to y before a vowel, evādhikāras fuses eva + adhikāraḥ (ḥ becomes s before t), and 'stv is astu, its a swallowed after o (ऽ) and its u turned to v.

lines.en: Your right is to action alone,
never to its fruits.

q.prompt: What does Arjuna have no claim to?

lines.en: Do not let the fruit of action be your motive,
nor cling to doing nothing.

q.prompt: Does Kṛṣṇa tell Arjuna to stop acting?
options: No, he must not cling to inaction
Yes, he should give up all action
Only once the battle is won

title: īśā vāsyam idaṃ sarvaṃ
about: The Īśa, one of the shortest Upaniṣads, is the last chapter of the White Yajurveda. It claims the whole moving world for the Lord and ends with a prayer to Pūṣan, a sun god, to uncover the face of truth. Words are printed apart: īśā vāsyam is the Kāṇva reading (often run together as īśāvāsyam), bhūtāny and ātmany are bhūtāni and ātmani with i turned to y before a vowel, evānupaśyati fuses eva + anupaśyati, cātmānaṃ is ca + ātmānam, satyasyāpihitaṃ is satyasya + apihitam, and pūṣann doubles its n before a vowel.

badge.name: Face of Truth
badge.about: Read verses of the Īśa Upaniṣad

lines.en: All this is to be dwelt in by the Lord,

q.prompt: Who is to dwell in all this?

lines.en: whatever moves in this moving world.
Enjoy it by giving it up;

q.prompt: How should one enjoy the world?
options: by owning as much as possible

lines.en: do not covet anyone's wealth.

lines.g: यस् तु सर्वाणि भूतान्य् आत्मन्य् एवानुपश्यति
lines.t: yas tu sarvāṇi bhūtāny ātmany evānupaśyati
lines.en: One who sees all beings in himself
and himself in all beings no longer recoils from anything.

q.prompt: What happens to someone who sees all beings in himself?

lines.en: The face of truth is hidden by a golden vessel.

lines.g: तत् त्वं पूषन्न् अपावृणु सत्यधर्माय दृष्टये
lines.t: tat tvaṃ pūṣann apāvṛṇu satyadharmāya dṛṣṭaye
lines.en: Uncover it, Pūṣan, so that I, whose law is truth, may see.
gloss: for one whose law is truth

q.prompt: What does the poet ask Pūṣan to do?

title: eko vṛddho vyāghraḥ
about: The Hitopadeśa, 'good advice', teaches princes through animal fables. In its first story a dove king warns his flock with this tale of an old tiger posing as a holy man: the kuśa grass in his paw is what priests hold during rites. Words are printed apart and compounds as one word: tāvan is tāvat before m, cintayann doubles its n before a vowel, and evāsau fuses eva + asau.

badge.name: Good Counsel
badge.about: Read the Hitopadeśa fable of the old tiger

lines.g: एको वृद्धो व्याघ्रः स्नातः कुशहस्तः सरस्तीरे ब्रूते
lines.t: eko vṛddho vyāghraḥ snātaḥ kuśahastaḥ sarastīre brūte
lines.en: An old tiger, freshly bathed and holding kuśa grass, calls from the shore of a lake:

q.prompt: How does the tiger present himself?
options: as a holy man, bathed and holding sacred grass
as a traveller with a staff

lines.g: भो भो पान्थाः इदं सुवर्णकङ्कणं गृह्यताम्
lines.t: bho bho pānthāḥ idaṃ suvarṇakaṅkaṇaṃ gṛhyatām
lines.en: 'Ho there, travellers! Take this golden bracelet.'
Then a traveller, drawn by greed, thought it over.

q.prompt: What draws the traveller to the tiger?

lines.en: 'Where is your bracelet?'
The tiger stretches out his paw and shows it.

lines.g: पान्थो ऽवदत् कथं मारात्मके त्वयि विश्वासः
lines.en: The traveller said, 'How can anyone trust a killer like you?'

lines.g: तद् अत्र सरसि स्नात्वा सुवर्णकङ्कणम् इदं गृहाण
lines.t: tad atra sarasi snātvā suvarṇakaṅkaṇam idaṃ gṛhāṇa
lines.en: 'So bathe here in the lake and take this golden bracelet.'

lines.g: ततो यावद् असौ तद्वचःप्रतीतो लोभात् सरः स्नातुं प्रविष्टः
lines.t: tato yāvad asau tadvacaḥpratīto lobhāt saraḥ snātuṃ praviṣṭaḥ
lines.en: As soon as the man, trusting his words, went into the lake out of greed to bathe,
he sank into deep mud and could not get away.

lines.g: इति चिन्तयन्न् एवासौ व्याघ्रेण धृत्वा व्यापादितः खादितश् च
lines.t: iti cintayann evāsau vyāghreṇa dhṛtvā vyāpāditaḥ khāditaś ca
lines.en: Still thinking this, he was seized by the tiger, killed and eaten.

q.prompt: What is the lesson of the fable?
options: greed makes you trust a killer
always bathe before taking a gift

title: āsīd rājā nalo nāma
about: In the forest, the sage Bṛhadaśva tells the exiled Yudhiṣṭhira about King Nala, who also lost his kingdom at dice. Damayantī is Bhīma's daughter, born after a sage's blessing. The tale has been a first reading for Western students since the early 1800s. Words are printed apart: iṣṭai is iṣṭaiḥ with its ḥ dropped before r, atiṣṭhan is atiṣṭhat with t turned to n before m, vedavic chūro is vedavit śūraḥ, tathaivāsīd fuses tathā + eva + āsīt, and cāprajaḥ is ca + aprajaḥ.

badge.name: King of Niṣadha
badge.about: Read the opening of the tale of Nala and Damayantī

lines.g: आसीद् राजा नलो नाम वीरसेनसुतो बली
lines.t: āsīd rājā nalo nāma vīrasenasuto balī
lines.en: There was a king named Nala, the mighty son of Vīrasena,

options: a king, the son of Vīrasena
a sage living in the forest

lines.en: blessed with every virtue one could wish, handsome, and expert with horses.
He stood at the head of the lords of men like Indra, lord of the gods,

q.prompt: Whom is Nala compared to among kings?

lines.g: उपर्य् उपरि सर्वेषाम् आदित्य इव तेजसा
lines.t: upary upari sarveṣām āditya iva tejasā
lines.en: far above them all, like the sun in splendour.
Devoted to brahmins, learned in the Veda, a hero, he ruled the land of the Niṣadhas,
fond of dice, true to his word, a great commander of armies.

q.prompt: Which of Nala's traits hints at trouble to come?

lines.en: Likewise, among the Vidarbhas there was Bhīma, of fearsome valour,

lines.g: शूरः सर्वगुणैर् युक्तः प्रजाकामः स चाप्रजः
lines.t: śūraḥ sarvaguṇair yuktaḥ prajākāmaḥ sa cāprajaḥ
lines.en: a hero with every virtue, who longed for children but had none.

lines.g: दमयन्ती तु रूपेण तेजसा यशसा श्रिया
lines.t: damayantī tu rūpeṇa tejasā yaśasā śriyā
lines.en: Damayantī, through her beauty, radiance, glory and grace

lines.g: सौभाग्येन च लोकेषु यशः प्राप सुमध्यमा
lines.t: saubhāgyena ca lokeṣu yaśaḥ prāpa sumadhyamā
lines.en: and charm, won fame throughout the worlds, the slender-waisted girl.
